headline: 9 Bangladeshis killed in Kolkata hotel fire
summary: A journalist from Kushtia and three of his family members are among the dead. The Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs is coordinating the repatriation of the bodies.
details: A devastating fire broke out at a residential hotel in Kolkata, India, resulting in the deaths of at least nine Bangladeshis.
Among the victims is Debashish, a journalist from Kushtia, who died along with his wife, child, and father-in-law.
The victims were reportedly staying at the hotel after completing medical treatment in the city before they were scheduled to return to Bangladesh.
The Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs has launched an emergency helpline for Bangladeshis in Kolkata to provide assistance during this crisis.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Shama Obaed, has assured that the bodies of the deceased will be repatriated to Bangladesh as quickly as possible.
The incident has raised serious concerns regarding the safety and fire security measures of hotels in Kolkata's New Market area.
caption:
A journalist from Kushtia and his family were killed in a horrific hotel fire in Kolkata.

A devastating fire broke out at a residential hotel in Kolkata, India, resulting in the deaths of at least nine Bangladeshis.

Among the victims is Debashish, a journalist from Kushtia, who died along with his wife, child, and father-in-law.

The victims were reportedly staying at the hotel after completing medical treatment in the city before they were scheduled to return to Bangladesh.

The Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs has launched an emergency helpline for Bangladeshis in Kolkata to provide assistance during this crisis.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Shama Obaed, has assured that the bodies of the deceased will be repatriated to Bangladesh as quickly as possible.

The incident has raised serious concerns regarding the safety and fire security measures of hotels in Kolkata's New Market area.

headline: Dipu Moni granted 12-hour parole to attend husband's funeral
summary: Former minister Dr Dipu Moni will be released from Munshiganj District Jail to bid farewell to her husband, Tawfique Nawaz, who passed away last night.
details: Former minister Dr Dipu Moni, a leader of the Awami League, will be released on parole from Munshiganj District Jail tomorrow morning. She has been granted a 12-hour window to attend the funeral of her husband, Tawfique Nawaz.
The release will take place at 6:00 am and she will remain on parole until 6:00 pm, according to Additional District Magistrate Md Rezaul Karim.
Dipu Moni's daughter, Tani Dipabali, had applied for parole for her mother after visiting her in prison this afternoon.
Dr Dipu Moni will visit her husband's body at their home in Kalabagan, Dhaka, before the janaza is held at Azad Mosque and burial at Banani Graveyard.
Tawfique Nawaz, a Supreme Court lawyer by profession, died at around 10:30 pm last night at Continental Hospital in Gulshan, Dhaka.
He was 76 years old and had been suffering from long-term kidney and liver complications.
caption:
Former minister Dipu Moni granted 12 hours of freedom from jail to attend her husband's funeral.

Former minister Dr Dipu Moni, a leader of the Awami League, will be released on parole from Munshiganj District Jail tomorrow morning. She has been granted a 12-hour window to attend the funeral of her husband, Tawfique Nawaz.

The release will take place at 6:00 am and she will remain on parole until 6:00 pm, according to Additional District Magistrate Md Rezaul Karim.

Dipu Moni's daughter, Tani Dipabali, had applied for parole for her mother after visiting her in prison this afternoon.

Dr Dipu Moni will visit her husband's body at their home in Kalabagan, Dhaka, before the janaza is held at Azad Mosque and burial at Banani Graveyard.

Tawfique Nawaz, a Supreme Court lawyer by profession, died at around 10:30 pm last night at Continental Hospital in Gulshan, Dhaka.

He was 76 years old and had been suffering from long-term kidney and liver complications.
